name: SplashSend for WooCommerce
author: splashsendteam

sections.description:
SplashSend is email marketing for shops. This plugin connects your WooCommerce shop to your SplashSend account.

  • Orders come across as they happen. Each buyer arrives in SplashSend’s People with what they bought, so a drip can thank a first-time buyer or ask for a review once the order ships.
  • A tick box at checkout. It starts unticked, and only buyers who tick it can be emailed. It works on the classic checkout and the block checkout.
  • Baskets left at checkout. Once you switch it on, when someone already on your list leaves their basket at checkout, SplashSend can send a reminder with a link that puts the same products back in their basket.
  • Your products in your emails. Products come across with their pictures, prices and links, ready for product blocks in your designs.
  • Your forms on your site. The SplashSend form block shows a sign-up form, a Collect form or a review wall on any page.
  • Website tracking. Once you switch it on, SplashSend’s script notices what people from your emails look at, so a drip can follow up. It follows your cookie banner through the WP Consent API.

You need a SplashSend account to use this plugin. You can sign up free at splashsend.com.

External services

This plugin connects your shop to SplashSend (splashsend.com), the email marketing service it was made for. Until you connect a SplashSend account, the only thing it loads from splashsend.com is a form you add with the SplashSend form block.

  • Connecting. When you select Connect to SplashSend, you sign in on splashsend.com and choose Allow, and SplashSend gives the plugin access to your account. The plugin asks splashsend.com for your account’s name when it connects, once a day, and when you open its page in WooCommerce, which keeps the connection working.
  • Orders. When an order is placed, and each time it changes, the plugin sends splashsend.com the order number and date, the buyer’s name, email address and IP address, what they bought, the total and currency, the order’s status, any coupon codes used, and whether they ticked the box at checkout. Bring in past orders sends older orders the same way.
  • Products. When you connect, and whenever a product changes, the plugin sends each product’s name, description, picture, price, stock, category, tags, link and whether it’s published.
  • Baskets left at checkout. Off until you switch on basket reminders in WooCommerce, then SplashSend. While it’s on, when a shopper gives their email address at checkout and leaves without ordering, the plugin sends splashsend.com that address, the products in the basket and a link back to it half an hour later. SplashSend only acts on it if the address is already on your list.
  • Website tracking. Off until you switch it on in WooCommerce, then SplashSend. While it’s on, your shop’s pages load SplashSend’s script from splashsend.com. It notes the products looked at and added to the basket by people who arrived from your SplashSend emails. With a cookie banner that uses the WP Consent API, it waits until the visitor allows marketing.
  • Forms. A page with the SplashSend form block loads that form from splashsend.com, and what a visitor types into the form goes to SplashSend.

Disconnecting, or deleting the plugin, tells splashsend.com to end the plugin’s access.

See SplashSend’s terms and privacy policy.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins, then Add New Plugin. Search for SplashSend, select Install Now, then Activate.
  2. Go to WooCommerce, then SplashSend, and select Connect to SplashSend.
  3. Sign in to SplashSend and choose Allow. You’ll come back to WordPress, connected.
  4. To bring in orders from before you connected, select Bring in past orders. They don’t start any drips or send any emails.

Your site needs an https address to connect.
sections.faq:
Does the tick box start ticked?

No. It starts unticked for every shopper, and you can change what it says in WooCommerce, then SplashSend.

What happens to buyers who don’t tick the box?

They arrive in SplashSend as customers who can’t be emailed, so nobody gets emails they didn’t ask for. If they sign up later, through one of your forms for example, they can be.

Will a reminder go to someone who bought after all?

No. A basket only counts as left once it has sat for half an hour with no order, and a reminder stops as soon as an order comes in.

Can I disconnect?

Yes. Select Disconnect in WooCommerce, then SplashSend, or remove the app in SplashSend under Apps. The people and orders already in SplashSend stay there.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • Browser notifications: the plugin can serve the small file your SplashSend notifications need, from your shop’s own address. It’s off until you switch it on in WooCommerce, then SplashSend.

1.1.2

  • Basket reminders and website tracking are off until you switch them on in WooCommerce, then SplashSend.

1.1.1

  • Small fixes from WordPress.org’s Plugin Check.

1.1.0

  • Sends the coupon codes each order used, so SplashSend can count how often its discount codes are used.

1.0.0

  • First version.
